notes:
Tier 1 (direct HTTP fetch, curl + HTML/breadcrumb-JSON parsing) sufficed; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (only /Files/Papirkurv/ and a cartcmd query pattern blocked), so no need to escalate. Discovery path: homepage top nav (/en) -> found 'Christmas' as the only seasonal item in the primary mega-menu; verified against the site's full category-index page (/en/products/category, a flat 130-link listing of every live category) which confirms 'christmas' and 'easter' are the only seasonal branches in the current taxonomy - no halloween/valentine/diwali/thanksgiving/new-year/eid/holi paths exist (all return 404 on direct guess, and none appear in the index). Also checked the Danish nav (/da/forside) for local-language seasonal terms - only 'jul' (Christmas) is promoted there, matching the English site; no separate Danish-only holiday branch found. Ran a same-server search test on mothers-day/black-friday guesses per shared engine discipline (see below) rather than trusting only the index page.

CHRISTMAS: main /en/products/christmas listing is itself a real PLP (title 'Bloomingville Christmas Collection', PageSize=12, pagination to PageNum=33, last page has 9 items -> 393 products) but its 8 genuine sub-category PLPs sum to only 336 (57 fewer), i.e. the subcategories are a proper subset of the parent listing (some Christmas-tagged products sit only at the group level, not under any subcategory) - textbook parent/children-are-subsets pattern, so Christmas is recorded as a grouping row (qty null) and the 8 subcategories are recorded as leaves to avoid double-counting. Sub-category names taken verbatim from each page's own breadcrumb JSON-LD, not from URL slugs. One duplicate was found and dropped per the shared overlap rule: /en/products/christmas/advent-candle-holder canonicalizes to and returns byte-identical product IDs/pagination as /en/products/christmas/candle-holders (same GroupId 'CHRISTMAS-CANDLEHOLDERS,CHRISTMAS-LANTERNS', same 12 items on every page checked) - it is a legacy alias, not a distinct category, so only candle-holders is kept.

EASTER: /en/products/easter is a genuine PLP (breadcrumb Products > Easter, GroupId-driven listing, pagination to PageNum=9, last page 2 items -> 98 total) with two genuine sub-category PLPs (For the home: pagination to PageNum=3, last page 5 -> 29; For the table: pagination to PageNum=6, last page 3 -> 63; sum 92, again a proper subset of the 98-item parent), so Easter is recorded as a grouping row and the two sub-categories as leaves. Products shown are general glassware/tableware curated for Easter (not egg/bunny-themed items), but the site's own breadcrumb and dedicated URL path explicitly associate the listing with Easter, satisfying the site-taxonomy test.

MOTHER'S DAY: /en/products/mothers-day is live and fully functional (breadcrumb Products > Mother's Day, GroupId-driven pagination to PageNum=6, last page 9 items -> 69 total, no sub-categories) but is NOT linked from the current main nav, mega-menu, or the comprehensive /en/products/category index page (unlike Christmas and Easter, which both appear there) - it was found only by guessing the URL slug. Included as a valid row because it independently passes every element of the PLP test (real breadcrumb-confirmed category, real product grid, own URL, exact qty), but flagged for manual review since it is currently orphaned from discoverable navigation (plausibly a dormant seasonal branch outside its active promotional window, similar to how Christmas will presumably be promoted again closer to Q4).

EXCLUDED: /en/products/black-friday also resolves (200, self-canonical, breadcrumb Products > Black Friday) but currently lists 0 products and has no pagination - an emptied/inactive promotional-event page, and 'Black Friday Sale'-type pages are explicitly excluded as promotional per the ruleset even when populated; with zero products it also fails the base 'lists products' PLP test, so no row was created. Guessed slugs for halloween, valentine(s)/valentine-s-day, new-year/new-year-s-eve, thanksgiving, diwali, fathers-day, autumn, fall, winter, summer, spring, wedding, party, holiday-shop, festive, gifts all returned 404 - confirmed absent, not merely unsearched.
